findings.trigger: POST /api/translation/test with a JSON body where 'text' is not a string, e.g. {"text": 123} -> `data.get('text', '').strip()` raises AttributeError. This line sits before the try/except block that starts at line 281, so nothing in this file catches it; Flask returns its default 500 error page instead of the endpoint's usual `{'success': False, 'error': ...}` JSON shape that every other failure path in this file uses.
findings.suggestion: Coerce/validate 'text' (and target_language/source_language, which have the same problem) to str before calling string methods, or wrap the parsing in the same try/except that already exists lower down, so a malformed body gets the same JSON error contract as every other failure here.

findings.trigger: provider == 'microsoft' and the API answers HTTP 200 with a body that has no usable 'translations' entry (e.g. `[{}]` or `[]`) -> the inner `if resp_data[0].get("translations")` is false, execution falls through the outer `if status == 200 and resp_data:` block without returning, and the endpoint answers `{'success': False, 'error': 'Microsoft API error: HTTP 200'}` - an HTTP-error message for a call that did not have an HTTP error. The DeepL and Google branches above it do not have this gap: each returns unconditionally inside its single `if status == 200 and resp_data:` (DeepL falls back to `resp_data.get("translations", [{}])[0]`, so it always returns from inside the if).
findings.suggestion: Give the Microsoft branch a distinct message for '200 but no translations in the response' instead of reusing the generic 'HTTP {status}' error text used for real HTTP failures.

findings.trigger: PUT-toggling a pair to DISABLED (not just re-enabling it) -> `translation_service.reset_auto_disabled(pair_id)` still runs, unconditionally, for every successful toggle in either direction. The comment right above it ('Reset auto-disable if user re-enables') says this should only happen when re-enabling.
findings.suggestion: Either gate the call on `result.data['enabled']` being True, or fix the comment if resetting on every toggle (including disabling) is actually intended.
findings.unsure_why: The interaction between the config 'enabled' flag and the separately tracked 'auto_disabled' state lives in translation_service / translation_config_service, which are not part of this section's source, so I cannot tell whether resetting on a manual disable has any user-visible consequence (e.g. whether it silently gives a broken pair a fresh five-failure budget the next time it is re-enabled) or is harmless because 'enabled' is checked first everywhere that matters.

findings.trigger: Loading `cogs.auto_action_monitor`, `cogs.translation_monitor`, or `cogs.docker_control` raises anything outside `(IOError, OSError, PermissionError, RuntimeError, docker.errors.APIError, docker.errors.DockerException)` - e.g. a plain ImportError from a missing dependency, or an AttributeError/TypeError/ValueError bug surfacing during the cog's setup() (which is exactly the kind of error a real code bug produces, and is also what discord.py/py-cord's own ExtensionError family - ExtensionFailed, ExtensionNotFound, NoEntryPointError - are, none of which subclass RuntimeError). That exception is not caught by this except clause and is not logged by the `logger.error(f"Failed to load extension '{ext}': {e}")` line at all; it propagates straight out of load_extensions_step and, as far as this section shows, out of the whole startup sequence for that boot - so command sync, dynamic cooldowns, scheduler start, update notification and member-count initialization never run this cycle. The comment directly above ('We don't raise here to allow other extensions to load (e.g. if one fails)') does not hold for this class of failure.
findings.suggestion: Widen the except clause (or add a final `except Exception` that still logs via the same `logger.error(...)` line) so a genuine cog bug is reported the same way an IOError/OSError one is, instead of escaping uncaught.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see discord.py/py-cord's actual exception hierarchy for load_extension in this section, nor app/bot/startup_steps/sequence.py (imported by __init__.py but not included here), which might itself catch and retry. I also note StartupManager.handle_ready only sets `_initial_startup_done = True` after a successful run, so if this does escape, the next `on_ready` (e.g. after a gateway reconnect) would retry the whole sequence - which softens, but does not remove, the gap: a boot with no reconnect for a long time would simply run without a scheduler, cooldowns or synced commands, with only a generic 'Error in event on_ready' traceback in the log to show for it.

findings.trigger: rename_group() decides 404-vs-400 by testing `"There is no group called" in (result.error or "")` against the error text produced by services/config/group_service.py, a file not included in this section. If that wording ever changes (rewording, translation, a different phrasing for the same case), renaming a group that does not exist would silently be reported as 400 (bad request) instead of 404 (not found), and the page's two different error treatments (per the comment two lines below) would apply to the wrong case.
findings.suggestion: Have rename_group() return a typed/coded result (e.g. a NOT_FOUND enum or exception) from the service instead of matching on the English error string, so the two places cannot drift apart.
findings.unsure_why: group_service.py is not part of this section's source, so I cannot check whether its current error text still matches this substring - I can only point out that the two places are coupled by a literal string rather than by a shared, checkable contract.

notes: Scope note: app/bot/startup_steps/__init__.py imports cooldowns.py, diagnostics.py and sequence.py (apply_dynamic_cooldowns_step, run_port_diagnostics_step, run_startup_sequence), none of which are in this section's source/ or PLAN.txt, so I did not review them and could not confirm how run_startup_sequence handles an exception from a step (relevant to F4). test_translation (app/blueprints/translation_routes.py:199) has two independent issues, F1 and F2; I attached the verdict to F1 and record F2 here since the schema only allows one finding id per PLAN name. Everything else in the section (bootstrap/runtime wiring, bot factory/dependencies/events, all other startup_steps, token.py's multi-layer token resolution) matches its own comments and the guarantees in SPEC.md (Z8-style broad excepts here are all narrow and logged, not bare `except: pass`; B3/B5/B9/B13 are not touched by this section).
